name: Student Club DB v1 (2 tables)
description: Each student may join at most one club, so the club is just a column on the student. The starting point for normalisation: see what breaks when someone wants to join a second club.

name: Student Club DB v2 (3 tables)
description: The same school clubs, done properly: a ClubReg table resolves the many-to-many relationship, keyed on the pair (SID, CID).

name: Student Club DB v3 (4 tables)
description: Registration now carries a school year, so the key grows to three columns and each club's teacher moves into a ClubInfo table of its own.

name: Stationery Shop DB
description: A small shop: customers place orders, each order lists products, and every product belongs to a category. Five tables and four foreign keys.

name: Book Loan DB (4 tables)
description: A library, where a title and a physical copy are not the same thing: BOOK is the title, BKCOPY is a copy on the shelf, and LOAN records who borrowed which copy and when.

name: Lunch Delivery DB (4 tables)
description: Members order lunch: one main dish, a drink if they want one, stamped with the time. Some orders have no drink, and not every member has ordered.
